$$\phi_n : M \otimes A^{\otimes n} \otimes N \longrightarrow N \otimes A^{\otimes n} \otimes M$$

After reversal $\phi_n$, this first $A$ becomes the last $A$ in $N \otimes A^{\otimes n} \otimes M$, adjacent to $M$. Then $d_n$ applies the left action on $\hat{M}$, which is $A \otimes M \xrightarrow{\sigma} M \otimes A \xrightarrow{\rho_M} M$. The swap $\sigma$ is already built into the reversal $\phi_n$, so both sides agree.

- **$i = n$ (left action on $N$):** $d_n$ applies $\lambda_N: A \otimes N \to N$ to the last $A$ factor. After reversal, this becomes the first $A$ adjacent to $\hat{N}$. Then $d_0$ applies the right action on $\hat{N}$, which is $N \otimes A \xrightarrow{\sigma} A \otimes N \xrightarrow{\lambda_N} N$. Again the swap is built into $\phi_n$, so both sides agree.

- **$0 < i < n$ (multiplication):** $d_i$ applies $\mu: A \otimes A \to A$ to the $i$-th and $(i+1)$-th $A$ factors. After reversal, these become the $(n-i)$-th and $(n-i+1)$-th factors, but in reversed order. So $d_{n-i}$ applies $\mu$ to $a_{i+1} \otimes a_i$ instead of $a_i \otimes a_{i+1}$. For any simplicial object $X: \Delta^{\mathrm{op}} \to \mathcal{C}$, the opposite $X^{\mathrm{op}} = X \circ \iota^{\mathrm{op}}$ satisfies
$$|X^{\mathrm{op}}| = \mathrm{colim}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(X \circ \iota^{\mathrm{op}}) \simeq \mathrm{colim}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}} X = |X|,$$
since precomposing with an autoequivalence of the indexing category does not change the colimit (up to equivalence).

Therefore $M \otimes N$ and $\hat{N} \otimes \hat{M}$ are isomorphic as objects in $Sp$. $\blacksquare$
